articles.title: Hawkish Fed Comments Boost the Dollar
articles.summary: The dollar index (DXY00 ) rose by +0.20% on Monday. The dollar moved higher on Monday amid hawkish Fed comments. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee and St...
articles.body:
The dollar index (DXY00) rose by +0.20% on Monday. The dollar moved higher on Monday amid hawkish Fed comments. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the Fed may have to hike interest rates further to restore price stability. Dollar gains were limited on Monday after WTI crude oil prices plunged by more than -4%, which eased inflation expectations and could persuade the Fed to loosen monetary policy, a bearish factor for the dollar. Also, a stronger Chinese yuan undercut the dollar as the yuan climbed to a 3.5-year high on Monday.

Today's US economic news showed the Aug Chicago Fed national activity index fell -0.12 to -0.04, right on expectations.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said that to restore price stability, the Fed may need to raise interest rates further and narrow the gap between supply and demand, which could lead to drops in employment, wages, and growth.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said core inflation may be running 1 percentage point above the Fed's 2% target and that the Fed likely needs to hike interest rates further.

Markets are pricing in a 55% chance of a +25 bp Fed rate hike at the next FOMC meeting on October 27-28.

EUR/USD (^EURUSD) fell by -0.18% on Monday. The dollar's strength on Monday weighed on the euro. Also, Monday's decline in the 10-year German Bund yield to a 1-week low of 3.442% has weakened the euro's interest rate differentials.

However, Monday's -4% decline in crude oil prices supports the Eurozone economy and the euro, as Europe imports most of its energy. Also, Monday's monthly report from the Bundesbank was slightly hawkish and supportive of the euro as it projected stronger economic German growth in in Q4 with "persistently high" energy prices.

In its monthly report released on Monday, the German Bundesbank said Q3 GDP will expand only "modestly" in Q3 because of short-term drivers like low water levels in the Rhine River, but the economy is expected to grow at a "stronger" pace again in Q4 and will "remain on its current path to recovery." The Bundesbank added that "persistently high prices, not only for crude oil but also for natural gas and electricity, could amplify both direct and indirect effects and delay the return of the inflation rate to 2%."

articles.title: Micron's Memory Boom Is Facing a New Test
articles.summary: Micron revenue jumped to $41.46 billion last quarter from $9.3 billion a year earlier.
articles.body:
Micron Technology ( MU , Financials ) has been a major winner in the AI-driven memory boom with revenue and earnings increasing amid sustained demand for high-bandwidth memory.

Micron's sales last quarter was $41.46 billion, up dramatically from $9.3 billion a year earlier. Its bottom line was boosted by increased demand and improved memory pricing, with GAAP net income of $28.24 billion.

The crucial question is whether the boom can be maintained, or whether at some point more output will create excess supply and put the squeeze on pricing.

The market is still digesting additional capacity, says investor Millennial Dividends. Low finished inventories at Samsung and SK Hynix lead the investor to forecast that around 70% of memory manufactured in 2026 will be for data centers.

The investor also believes the three big providers of DRAM and HBM have sold all their capacity until next year, which could keep the memory market tight as AI infrastructure increases.

Demand for data centers is strong and new capacity coming online might set Micron's next development phase. Millennial Dividends says the combination is a tailwind to additional earnings growth and Micron isn't demanding on a fiscal 2027 value.

Wall Street has 29 Buy recommendations and one Hold at the moment, with an average 12-month price goal of $ 1,564.44.

The next driver is whether Micron can keep pricing power when new memory capacity is added and AI demand continues to swallow supply.

articles.title: EUA barram participação da China em negociação com Brasil na OMC | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo americano afirma que disputa não envolve medidas contra produtos chineses e diz que Pequim não demonstrou interesse comercial substancial no caso.
articles.summary: Governo americano afirma que disputa não envolve medidas contra produtos chineses e diz que Pequim não demonstrou interesse comercial substancial no caso.
articles.body:
Os Estados Unidos rejeitaram o pedido da China para participar das consultas com o Brasil na Organização Mundial do Comércio ( OMC ) sobre as tarifas impostas pelo governo de Donald Trump a produtos brasileiros.

A decisão consta de um documento enviado pela delegação americana à OMC nesta terça-feira (22). Segundo os EUA, o pedido brasileiro não envolve atos, políticas ou práticas da China nem tarifas aplicadas a produtos de origem chinesa.

Por isso, o governo americano afirmou que não considera válida a alegação de Pequim de que tem um "interesse comercial substancial" na disputa e recusou o pedido.

A China havia solicitado a participação em 6 de agosto . Na ocasião, Pequim argumentou que uma das medidas questionadas pelo Brasil também afeta produtos chineses.

O pedido foi feito com base no artigo 4.11 do Entendimento sobre Solução de Controvérsias da OMC, que permite a participação de um terceiro país nas consultas quando ele demonstra ter interesse comercial substancial na questão.

Para isso, porém, é necessário que o país alvo da disputa concorde que o interesse é bem fundamentado.

Por que o Brasil foi à OMC, mesmo com o órgão enfraquecido?

A decisão tem um peso mais simbólico e institucional do que prático. Ao levar o caso à OMC, o Brasil formaliza a contestação às tarifas americanas e reforça a defesa das regras multilaterais de comércio, mesmo diante das limitações atuais do órgão para fazer suas decisões serem cumpridas.

O processo também mantém aberta uma via formal de negociação com os Estados Unidos e registra a posição brasileira dentro do sistema internacional de comércio.

Brasil e Estados Unidos têm consultas marcadas para esta sexta-feira (25), em Genebra, na Suíça.

As consultas são a primeira etapa do processo de solução de controvérsias da OMC e têm como objetivo tentar resolver a questão por meio de negociação.

Se não houver acordo, o Brasil poderá pedir a abertura de um painel para analisar a disputa.

articles.title: Embraer E2: Por que o avião brasileiro é um sucesso comercial? | G1
articles.standfirst: Instabilidade global no GPS afetou aeronaves da linha, que é formada por três modelos e tem ganhado espaço no mercado de aviação.
articles.summary: A linha Embraer E2 supera instabilidades de GPS e atrai aéreas globais com baixo consumo de combustível e prazos de entrega reduzidos.
articles.body:
Air Astana recebeu primeiro jato E190-E2 nesta sexta-feira (14) — Foto: Embraer/Divulgação

Uma instabilidade global no sistema de GPS afetou a operação dos aviões da linha E2 , da fabricante brasileira Embraer. O problema atingiu principalmente aeronaves da Azul , que opera esse tipo de avião em rotas pelo Brasil.

Segundo a Embraer, a instabilidade não compromete a segurança dos voos. A frota tem sistemas de navegação que permitem a operação mesmo quando há problemas no GPS.

A linha E2 é formada por três modelos: E175-E2 , E190-E2 e E195-E2 . Eles têm diferentes capacidades de passageiros, pesos e alcances. (Veja os detalhes na arte abaixo) .

A linha tem virado a galinha dos ovos de ouro da empresa brasileira, que tem sede em São José dos Campos, no interior de São Paulo. Segundo a revista britânica The Economist, o modelo tem ganhado destaque principalmente pela boa autonomia e pelo baixo consumo de combustível.

A revista lembra que, atualmente, as companhias aéreas precisam esperar até dez anos para receber um avião de fuselagem estreita (aqueles com apenas um corredor entre os assentos) de fabricantes como Airbus e Boeing, rivais da empresa brasileira.

A alta demanda por viagens aéreas e os problemas na cadeia de suprimentos, que persistem desde a pandemia de Covid-19, aumentaram a procura por aeronaves menores, como o E2 . Nesse cenário, a Embraer ganha espaço porque consegue entregar o modelo em menos de dois anos .

"O E2 é uma aeronave muito moderna. É um projeto já do século XXI, vamos dizer assim, que atrela muitas coisas que fazem esse avião ser diferenciado: projeto bem feito de massa, motores de nova geração (os mais modernos possíveis) e sistemas de navegação também muito modernos", explica ao g1 Bruno Chieregatti, engenheiro mecânico do Instituto Mauá de Tecnologia (IMT).

Segundo o especialista, a linha E2 tem uma capacidade de passageiros um pouco menor que os aviões da Boeing e da Airbus. "Mas nem todas as rotas precisam de capacidades tão elevadas, de 180 a 200 passageiros, que um Boeing e um Airbus precisam para ser viável economicamente".

"Ter uma aeronave com capacidade entre 140 e 150 passageiros, um pouco menor, faz com que as companhias tenham flexibilidade de fazer voos diferenciados", completa.

No Brasil, os aviões da família E2 são operados por Azul e Latam. A Gol também fechou a compra de 20 aeronaves E195-E2.

Em outros países, os modelos estão presentes na frota ou têm intenção de compra de companhias como Avelo Airlines, dos Estados Unidos; Finnair, da Finlândia; Star Air, da Índia; Luxair, de Luxemburgo; e Airlink, da África do Sul.

Como é o E2, avião da brasileira Embraer, e por que ele é considerado um sucesso comercial — Foto: Arte g1

articles.title: Feira de Profissões da UNITAU tem programação nos três períodos nesta semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento será realizado nos dias 23 e 24 de setembro, no Departamento de Comunicação e Negócios com atividades presenciais e transmissão online
articles.summary: Evento será realizado nos dias 23 e 24 de setembro, no Departamento de Comunicação e Negócios com atividades presenciais e transmissão online
articles.body:
A Universidade de Taubaté (UNITAU) realiza, nesta semana, mais uma edição da Feira de Profissões, nesta quarta-feira (23) e quinta-feira (24), com programação nos períodos da manhã, tarde e noite. O evento será realizado no Departamento de Comunicação e Negócios (CEN) e também contará com conteúdo, ampliando as possibilidades de participação de estudantes interessados em conhecer as opções de formação oferecidas pela Universidade. As inscrições devem ser feitas em unitau.br/feiradeprofissoes.

Durante os dois dias, os participantes poderão conhecer os cursos de graduação da UNITAU, conversar com professores e estudantes, visitar espaços acadêmicos e participar de atividades preparadas especialmente para apresentar, na prática, diferentes áreas de atuação profissional. A edição de 2025 reuniu mais de 4 mil pessoas, a expectativa dos organizadores é que neste ano, o evento conte com cerca de 5 mil visitantes.

Para a Pró-reitoria de Graduação da UNITAU, a Feira é uma oportunidade para que os estudantes tenham contato mais próximo com a Universidade e possam refletir sobre a escolha profissional.

“A Feira de Profissões é um momento importante para aproximar os estudantes da Universidade e ajudá-los a conhecer diferentes possibilidades de formação. Mais do que apresentar cursos, queremos proporcionar experiências que permitam aos participantes entender melhor cada área, conversar com quem vive a graduação e começar a construir, com mais informação, os próximos passos de sua trajetória”, destaca.

A programação foi organizada para receber estudantes em diferentes horários ao longo dos dois dias, permitindo que escolas e participantes individuais escolham o período mais adequado para a visita.

Além das atividades presenciais, como júri simulado, oficinas práticas e orientação profissional, a Feira também contará com uma programação online, ampliando o acesso para quem não puder participar presencialmente. O conteúdo exclusivo aborda temas como criatividade, gestão financeira, elaboração de currículo, saúde mental e robótica na indústria. Os participantes inscritos também poderão acessar os conteúdos posteriormente.

O Departamento de Comunicação e Negócios (CEN) está localizado na Rua Expedicionário Ernesto Pereira, 225, no Centro de Taubaté.

Anote na agenda – Com infraestrutura moderna e equipamentos de ponta, a UNITAU abre, nesta quarta-feira (23), as inscrições para o Vestibular de Verão 2027. O processo seletivo oferece oportunidades em diversos cursos de graduação, entre eles Medicina, Direito e Pedagogia, que recebeu nota 5 na última edição do Exame Nacional de Desempenho dos Estudantes (Enade).

Os interessados em Medicina podem consultar informações e realizar a inscrição pelo site unitau.br/medicina . Para os demais cursos, as inscrições estão disponíveis em unitau.br/vestibular .

articles.title: Preço médio da passagem aérea chega a R$ 777, maior valor desde 2024 | G1
articles.standfirst: Tarifa média subiu 14,5% entre agosto de 2025 e 2026. No mês, também caiu a parcela de passagens vendidas por até R$ 500, enquanto o combustível de aviação ficou mais caro.
articles.summary: Tarifa média subiu 14,5% entre agosto de 2025 e 2026. No mês, também caiu a parcela de passagens vendidas por até R$ 500, enquanto o combustível de aviação ficou mais caro.
articles.body:
Viajar de avião ficou mais caro no Brasil em agosto. A tarifa aérea real média no mercado doméstico chegou a R$ 776,87 , o maior valor desde dezembro de 2024, quando ficou em R$ 813,80, segundo dados da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac).

O valor também é 14,5% maior do que o registrado no mesmo mês do ano passado. Em relação ao mês anterior, quando a tarifa era de R$ 701,27, a alta foi de 10,8%.

A chamada tarifa aérea real média corresponde ao valor médio pago pelo passageiro pelo serviço de transporte aéreo. O cálculo é corrigido pela inflação medida pelo IPCA, com referência em agosto de 2026.

🔎 A tarifa de embarque e outros serviços adicionais, como bagagem despachada e marcação de assento, não estão incluídos nesse valor.

Os dados mostram também que, em agosto, houve uma redução na participação das passagens mais baratas. Entre julho de 2024 e agosto de 2026, 47,2% dos assentos foram vendidos por até R$ 500. Apenas em agosto, essa parcela ficou em 34,8% .

Isso significa que, naquele mês, uma proporção menor dos assentos foi comercializada por até R$ 500, o que contribuiu para elevar o preço médio das passagens.

Outro indicador acompanhado pela Anac mostra uma alta no preço do querosene de aviação (QAV), um dos principais custos das companhias aéreas. Em agosto, o preço chegou a R$ 4,98 por litro, alta de 18,8% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025.

O aumento do combustível ocorreu ao mesmo tempo em que a tarifa aérea média subiu. O QAV tem peso nos custos das companhias e, consequentemente, na formação do preço das passagens.

Valor pago por quilômetro também aumentou

Outro indicador da Anac, chamado yield aéreo real , também apresentou alta. O yield mede quanto, em média, as companhias recebem por passageiro a cada quilômetro voado.

Entre julho de 2024 e agosto de 2026, a média do indicador foi de R$ 0,5201 por quilômetro. Apenas em agosto, o valor ficou em R$ 0,5834 por quilômetro, 12,2% acima dessa média.

🔎 Assim, além de a tarifa média ter aumentado, também houve crescimento do valor médio associado a cada quilômetro percorrido pelo passageiro.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta, com negociações entre EUA e Irã no radar; Ibovespa cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana recuou 0,11%, cotada a R$ 5,1028. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,46%, aos 187.457 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana recuou 0,11%, cotada a R$ 5,1028. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,46%, aos 187.457 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em alta nesta quarta-feira (23), com um avanço de 0,61% perto das 10h10, cotado a R$ 5,1340 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha queda de 0,73% no mesmo horário, aos 186.051 pontos .

Com foco no exterior, investidores continuam a monitorar as negociações entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã e seguem em compasso de espera pelo encontro entre os presidentes Donald Trump e Xi Jinping , prevista para quinta-feira. Na agenda doméstica, uma terceira rodada de pesquisas eleitorais da Quaest fica sob os holofotes.

▶️ Os sinais de avanço nas negociações entre EUA e Irã seguem no centro das atenções. Na véspera, Trump afirmou que autoridades dos dois países se encontraram para as tratativas, em uma reunião que durou cerca de três horas. O Irã também indicou que pode reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz em sete dias se os americanos alivirarem a pressão militar e suspenderem o bloqueio aos portos iranianos.

Perto das 10h10, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 1,30% , cotado a US$ 100,54 . Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência nos EUA, tinha alta de 0,68% no mesmo horário, a US$ 91,14 o barril.

▶️ No cenário eleitoral, a Quaest deve divulgar uma terceira rodada de pesquisas nesta quarta-feira. O último levantamento mostrou que Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão empatados no limite da margem de erro no 1º turno. Lula está à frente, com 37%, e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) chega a 33%. Com a margem de erro de dois pontos, Lula pode ter de 35% a 39%, enquanto Flávio pode ter entre 31% e 35%.

▶️ Os mercados também seguiram em compasso de espera pela cúpula entre Trump e Xi Jinping, prevista para quinta-feira. A expectativa é que os líderes sinalizem uma prorrogação da trégua comercial firmada entre os dois países no ano passado e que evitou um grande choque na economia global. Questões envolvendo Taiwan também podem ser abordadas.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Os sinais de avanço nas tratativas entre EUA e Irã seguem no radar dos investidores. Na terça-feira, o presidente americano, Donald Trump, afirmou que pode "aniquilar o Irã" e mandar o país "para o inferno" em discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova York.

Poucas horas mais tarde, porém, anunciou que autoridades iranianas e americanas se reuniram também nesta terça para negociar. "Foi uma reunião de três horas", disse o presidente americano a jornalistas. Trump descreveu o encontro como "muito bom" e afirmou que planeja outro diálogo "em um futuro muito próximo".

Durante seu discurso na ONU, Trump defendeu a guerra no Oriente Médio e reiterou que o Irã "nunca terá uma arma nuclear". Ele também disse que tem uma "grande decisão" pela frente.

"Um acordo será feito com o Irã para que eles consigam reconstruir um grande país, como já foi antes, talvez um dos maiores países no Oriente Médio, ou será que eu tenho que aniquilar a República Islâmica para o inferno e rapidamente? Vamos tentar fazer um acordo logo após as eleições", afirmou Trump.

O Irã, por sua vez, disse que pode reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz em sete dias se os Estados Unidos aliviarem a pressão militar e suspenderem o bloqueio aos portos iranianos.

A delegação iraniana que viajou para participar da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova York, tem plena autoridade para retomar as relações diplomáticas com os EUA.

Esta semana, o Irã entregou aos EUA, por meio de mediadores, uma nova proposta de acordo para dar fim às hostilidades entre os dois países.

Os mercados financeiros também seguem na expectativa pela cúpula entre os presidentes Donald Trump e Xi Jinping , prevista para quinta-feira.

Além da prorrogação do acordo comercial, os dois países também devem tratar sobre inteligência artificial.

Estados Unidos e China consideram os avanços na tecnologia estratégicos para a competitividade econômica e militar dos dois países. Washington e Pequim, no entanto, mantêm divergências importantes sobre o setor.

Entre os principais pontos de atrito estão as restrições americanas ao acesso da China a chips avançados, acusações envolvendo cópia e transferência de tecnologia e diferenças sobre como a indústria de inteligência artificial deve ser regulada.

Os Estados Unidos têm restringido o acesso chinês a semicondutores de ponta e outras tecnologias consideradas estratégicas, enquanto a China critica as medidas e acusa Washington de tentar limitar seu desenvolvimento tecnológico.

Na Ásia , a maioria dos mercados fechou em queda, conforme investidores avaliavam papéis de tecnologia e em meio à expectativa de que a China e os EUA prorroguem a trégua comercial na reunião entre Trump e Xi Jinping, prevista para quinta-feira.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, caiu 0,39%, enquanto o CSI300 , que reúne as maiores empresas das bolsas de Xangai e Shenzhen, perdeu 0,60%. Já o Hang Seng, de Hong Kong , recuou 1,01% e o Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, subiu 0,90%. O Nikkei , do Japão, permaneceu fechado.

articles.title: Oil prices ease as Saudi Arabia restores key pipeline, traders remain optimistic on US-Iran talks
articles.summary: International Business News: Oil prices slipped below the $100-a-barrel mark on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supplies through a key pipeline to the Red Sea, whi.
articles.body: Oil prices slipped below the $100-a-barrel mark on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supplies through a key pipeline to the Red Sea, while hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran war added to the ease.WTI crude was trading at $90.10 a barrel, down 42 cents, or 0.46%, while Brent crude stood at $99.09, down 16 cents, or 0.16% around 7:30 am IST.The decline came after Brent closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8. Expectations of improving oil supplies, along with efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the nearly seven-month conflict, put pressure on benchmark crude prices.US President Donald Trump has warned that he could "annihilate" Iran, but also said his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held productive talks with Iranian mediators aimed at ending the war."I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal," Trump said.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has restarted operations on its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, according to three sources briefed on the matter. The move has been accompanied by signs of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.The pipeline had been shut on September 11 after drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia blamed on an Iraqi militia, halted crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf producers through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels of crude per day to Yanbu. That volume is equivalent to around 4% of global oil supply.Iraq is also increasing its oil exports. Oil minister Basim Mohammed said on Tuesday that the country was exporting more than 3 million barrels per day and expected exports through Turkey to rise to more than 600,000 bpd.Provisional figures from shiptracking firms Vortexa and Kpler put Iraq's crude exports in August at 2.3 million bpd and 2.17 million bpd, respectively. Both estimates were higher than July levels but remained below the February pre-war levels of 3.7 million bpd and 3.362 million bpd, respectively.Adding to the pressure on oil prices, industry data showed US crude inventories increased by 1.8 million barrels in the week to September 18. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected inventories to decline.As the conflict continues for over 6 months now, oil markets have continued to remain volatile as global supply chains continue to face disruption.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Sebi may review expiry-day settlement price mechanism
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Tuesday said the capital markets regulator intends to address concerns over the settlement price for de.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Tuesday said the capital markets regulator intends to address concerns over the settlement price for derivatives on expiry days and other related issues.To address market participants' concerns, Sebi floated a consultation paper earlier this month seeking public comments on the proposed changes to the methodology for determining expiry-day settlement prices of index and single-stock derivatives. The proposals include delinking derivatives' settlement prices from the cash-market closing price, discontinuing live indicative index values during the CAS (Closing Auction Session) and making orders placed beyond the 1% band more binding."Having successfully established the CAS as an important market structure reform, we intend to address concerns in respect of settlement price for derivatives on expiry days and other related issues. A consultation paper has already been issued inviting public comment," Pandey said at the 11th JP Morgan India Conference.The regulator proposed two options for determining the settlement price. Under the first, called Blended VWAP, the settlement price would be based on transactions executed during the last 30 minutes of the Continuous Trading Session (CTS) and the 10-minute CAS. The contribution of each period would be based on its actual traded value, with no fixed weight assigned to either.Under the second option, Sebi proposed continuing with the existing CTS Volume weighted average price (VWAP) methodology, under which only trades executed during the last 30 minutes of CTS would be considered. The regulator said the CTS VWAP could be retained as an interim methodology to provide continuity and allow market participants more time to familiarise themselves with CAS.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday said that the Indian economy is expanding close to 8%, while global growth has slowed below .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday said that the Indian economy is expanding close to 8%, while global growth has slowed below 3%, prompting the world to re-rate India.Addressing an AIMA event, she called for not just building bigger Indian companies, but better companies that are competitive, innovative, trusted and resilient to lead India into the future.In her address, FM underlined the need to help startups and MSMEs deal with succession planning, governance, conflict management and delegation, while calling for Indian business models."A large share of India's MSMEs and mid-sized enterprises are family owned. Many have strong products, loyal customers and significant growth potential, but expansion can be held back by unclear roles, succession disputes, informal decision making and disagreements within the family," said Sitharaman.She said the challenge is often not entrepreneurship, but institutionalisation and this can be achieved by overhauling management curricula for today's techno-economic realities. "We need professionalisation: separating ownership from management, defining responsibilities, preparing the next generation, and resolving conflicts before they affect the business itself."Sitharaman highlighted that over the next two decades, the challenge is not simply to keep creating more startups, it is to see how many of them can become large, professionally managed and enduring corporations. "AIMA can make these enterprises make the difficult transition from founder-led ventures to institution-led companies - without losing the entrepreneurial energy that created them in the first place," said Sitharaman.She also emphasised that sound corporate governance is not simply a set of external codes to be adopted, as it depends on the standards institutions set for themselves."Businesses must engage constructively with govt and regulators. Legal recourse will always remain available, but every disagreement need not begin as litigation. There is considerable value in engaging early, placing evidence on the table, participating seriously in consultations and working towards solutions before differences become disputes," she noted.She also said Indian industry needs to build institutions that combine scale with durability, higher quality, better governance and deeper technological capabilities.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court's order, seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, has created a reputational overhang and weighs on investor confidence.The Aug 31 high court order came in a case arising from Japanese firm Daiichi Sankyo's efforts to enforce its arbitral award against the erstwhile Fortis promoters. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in SC, challenging the order.Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold 57% shareholding, while retail share is over 11% in the company. "The question for the market is whether a transaction that has cleared the entire approval architecture - board, shareholders, CCI, Sebi, the takeover code, ever becomes settled'', Shriram Subramanian MD and founder of InGovern, a proxy advisory firm, told TOI.In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore. "Questioning a transaction long cleared by all regulators and seeking its forensic audit after nearly a decade, will open a can of worms,'' he added.IHH is a credible strategic investor, and Fortis, after years of promoter-related turmoil and uncertainty, is now on a more stable footing, investors feel, and prolonged legal proceedings could create uncertainty. While the court has made clear that the forensic audit is a fact-finding exercise and does not, by itself, impose liability, investors said the process could still have wider implications for the company."Capital is mobile and investors have alternatives; prolonged uncertainty can therefore have consequences for the company and its shareholders,'' InGovern said in a note.The acquisition was approved by the board, cleared by the CCI, and completed under the Sebi takeover regulations through an open offer that market regulator itself permitted. articles.title: Russian oligarch’s wedding gift to Trump Jr puts family dealings under scrutiny
articles.summary: International Business News: A Russian oligarch’s role in Donald Trump Jr’s wedding celebrations has now sparked a call for a Senate investigation from the GOP. Republican senator.
articles.body: A Russian oligarch’s role in Donald Trump Jr’s wedding celebrations has now sparked a call for a Senate investigation from the GOP. Republican senator John Curtis of Utah has asked the Judiciary Committee to examine whether US president Donald Trump’s son benefited financially from his proximity to the White House.Curtis, who is not a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, made the request in a letter sent on Tuesday to committee chairman Chuck Grassley, a Republican from Iowa, and the panel’s top Democrat, Illinois Senator Dick Durbin. He asked the committee to subpoena Trump Jr over his business dealings, relationships with foreign individuals and entities, gifts and other benefits he has received, and any instances in which his relationship with President Donald Trump “was invoked or understood to provide value.”Curtis also called for the same scrutiny of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden.“The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president,” Curtis wrote.Curtis seeks scrutiny of Jr's foreign tiesThe request puts a Republican senator at the centre of scrutiny of Trump’s family at a time when most Republican lawmakers have largely avoided weighing in on the president’s son.Curtis, who was first elected to the Senate in 2024, has previously vowed not to shy away from disagreements with Trump. He has publicly broken with the president several times, including rejecting Trump’s calls to eliminate the Senate filibuster.His latest criticism, however, goes beyond a disagreement over policy. Curtis last Friday described the reported wedding funding as “corruption” and said he would say more about the issue in the coming days.“A Russian oligarch paid for a lavish wedding after-party for Donald Trump Jr, which to me just stinks. It’s corruption. I don’t like it,” Curtis said in a video posted on social media.Earlier on Tuesday, Curtis also referred to the Republican-led scrutiny of Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships, writing that Republicans “nearly wore out the subpoena machine investigating Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships” and that they “should not unplug it now.”Russian oligarch helped fund wedding celebrationsThe controversy follows a report by ProPublica last week that Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin, helped pay for the rental of a private island and a fireworks show during celebrations for Trump Jr and socialite Bettina Anderson’s wedding in the Bahamas in May.Bettina Trump later addressed Kremlev’s involvement in an Instagram post signed by the couple. She described Kremlev, who is head of the International Boxing Association, as a “dear friend” who “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding.”Though Trump did not attend his son’s wedding, he defended Kremlev’s involvement but said the money would be paid back.Curtis’ letter asks the Judiciary Committee to examine Trump Jr’s business dealings, his relationships with foreign individuals and entities, and gifts or other benefits he has received. It also seeks scrutiny of instances in which his relationship with the president “was invoked or understood to provide value.”More facts neededGrassley has not yet committed to an investigation. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, he said he was not yet familiar with the facts surrounding the case and would need to gather more information before deciding what action to take.“I’m going to take these requests seriously and sit down with staff and see what we can do,” Grassley said.He added that the process would take time and said, “it takes time, and if you were going to ask me when we're going to have a hearing, there’s no way I could answer that today.”Senate majority leader John Thune, Republican of South Dakota, also declined to offer a view, saying he did not “have an observation on that.”Still, some Republican lawmakers have indicated that they would support Curtis’ request.The developments come as a few Republicans have recently shown a greater willingness to criticise Trump’s policies after largely avoiding public breaks with him during much of his second term.Meanwhile, the ongoing war in Iran, high gas prices and mounting concerns about Republican prospects in November’s midterm elections have brought increased scrutiny of the president from within his own party.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Costco has the luxury of sitting out the delivery arms race
articles.summary: People want the thrill of the Costco treasure hunt more than same-day delivery.
articles.body:
Costco Wholesale last week announced a new partnership with DoorDash and a major extension of its relationship with Uber , vastly expanding its same-day delivery firepower but nonetheless leaving it well behind rivals like Walmart and Amazon , which use drones for some of their fast deliveries. And that is by design.

Until now, Costco's same-day delivery has consisted largely of teaming up with Instacart for very quick delivery, typically groceries and other essentials. (For two-day delivery, Costco typically handles shipping itself.) And while the Uber and DoorDash tie-ups give Costco much more reach, the moves also serve as a reminder that Costco's business model and the intense, almost cult-like customer loyalty the membership-based retailer inspires mean that it doesn't have to participate in the delivery arms race the same way its rivals do.

Costco fanatics don't shop there because of fast delivery. They shop there for its curated assortment, competitive prices, its highly trusted Kirkland Signature brand, and the treasure-hunt aspect of shopping in its cavernous warehouses; they might stumble across a jar of luxurious La Mer moisturizer while looking for underwear or croutons.

Such is Costco's hold on its satisfied customers that 92.3% of members in the U.S. and Canada renewed last year. Costco's net sales for the fiscal year ended in August hit $297.3 billion, nearly triple what they were a decade ago.

"E-commerce is important to Costco, but it's not the be-all and end-all in the way it is for some businesses. Costco is also quite well differentiated so while it does compete with Amazon and Walmart, it isn't quite as involved in the digital grocery battle that those two are fighting," said Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData.

What's more, Costco's business model is designed for its basic retail operations to be break-even, so that it can continue to offer the low prices members seek. Indeed, most years, Costco's membership revenue is roughly equivalent to its net income. The average Costco store carries about 4,000 different items, compared to 100,000 at Walmart. That selectivity gives Costco clout with vendors to get low prices.

Its margins, low by design, mean that Costco has to be very careful about how it spends money, hence its decision to team up with other companies for its same-day delivery rather than build out its own infrastructure like Walmart (including its Sam's Club business, which competes directly with Costco), Target , and Amazon. It's a particularly important consideration for Costco and Sam's Club given how heavy deliveries from these bulk retailers can be and why they steer customers toward curbside delivery as much as possible.

articles.title: He surrendered tenancy rights for redevelopment and got 2 flats worth Rs 1.38 crore; taxman added it as income, why ITAT Mumbai gave him relief
articles.summary: India Business News: This is the case of a man who surrendered his tenancy rights and got flats from the builder in lieu of that. He was then served an income tax notice f.
articles.body: This is the case of a man who surrendered his tenancy rights and got flats from the builder in lieu of that. He was then served an income tax notice for the same. He fought a long battle, and finally won relief from ITAT Mumbai.He was a tenant in Mumbai in a housing society that was slated to undergo redevelopment. He received two flats in the redeveloped building in return for surrendering his tenancy rights.The tribunal ruled that a tax demand under Section 56(2)(x) could not be imposed on the individual merely because he received two flats in exchange for giving up his tenancy rights in the redevelopment project.What the case is aboutThe man had been a tenant of four shops in a Mumbai housing society. When the society opted for redevelopment, he entered into a permanent alternative agreement (PAA) with the builder.Under the arrangement, the man agreed to surrender his existing tenancy rights. In return, the builder was to provide him with two flats in the redeveloped building as permanent alternate accommodation.The two flats provided to him under the PAA were valued at Rs 1.38 crore by the stamp duty authorities, according to an ET report.The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) from Parel, however, invoked Section 56(2)(x) and treated the entire stamp duty value of Rs 1.38 crore as "income from other sources" in the tenant’s hands. This resulted in the tenant becoming liable to pay income tax on the amount.Section 56(2)(x) applies where a person receives an asset, including property, without consideration or for inadequate consideration exceeding Rs 50,000, with the resulting amount being taxed under the head "Income from other sources".In this case, the tax notice arose because the Income Tax Department proceeded on the basis that he had received the two flats without consideration. His position, however, was that the flats were provided to him as part of the redevelopment arrangement after he surrendered his existing tenancy rights.The matter subsequently went before the Commissioner of Appeals (CIT(A)), which upheld the addition made by the Assessing Officer. The CIT(A) took the view that, in substance, the tenant had received valuable immovable property in return for extinguishing his tenancy rights.The CIT(Appeals) further held that execution and registration of the redevelopment agreements had resulted in the man acquiring absolute ownership rights in the alternate premises. According to the appellate authority, those rights could not subsequently be changed without his consent.On this basis, the CIT(Appeals) concluded that the property had been received during the relevant assessment year, even though physical possession of the flats had not yet been handed over.The CIT(Appeals) also agreed with the Assessing Officer's decision to apply Section 56(2)(x). It held that the tenant had obtained valuable immovable property without providing adequate monetary consideration and therefore confirmed the addition of Rs 1.38 crore to his income.The man challenged this decision before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Mumbai. On July 16, 2026, the ITAT ruled in his favour.Why did the tenant win the case in ITAT Mumbai?Mihir Tanna, associate director, S.K Patodia LLP, told ET that the Mumbai ITAT had considered a similar issue in March 2026 in the case of Varun Jaisingh Asher, although the facts were different.Tanna explained that tenancy rights are treated as a capital asset and surrendering such rights amounts to a transfer that is taxable under the capital gains provisions.He said that when a property is allotted under a redevelopment arrangement, the allotment represents the consideration received in return for giving up those tenancy rights.Tanna says: “Therefore, the transaction squarely falls within the ambit of capital gains and cannot be brought to tax under the residuary provisions of Section 56(2)(x)”The tenant’s contention was that he had not actually received the alternate premises because construction of the redevelopment project was still underway and possession had not been given to him.He also maintained that the allotment of the new units could not be treated as a property received without consideration. The permanent alternate accommodation was being provided by the builder in return for the surrender of his valuable tenancy rights.The central question before the Mumbai ITAT was whether Section 56(2)(x) could be applied simply because the redevelopment agreements had been executed and registered during the relevant assessment year, even though construction remained incomplete and Devshichhadva had neither obtained possession nor acquired the right to enjoy the alternate premises.The ITAT Mumbai examined the requirement under Section 56(2)(x) that the taxpayer must "receive" immovable property during the relevant previous year. The tribunal held that the word "receives" could not be given an artificial or notional meaning that would result in taxation merely because a redevelopment agreement had been registered.Before the deeming provision could be applied, the tribunal said, there had to be an actual receipt of the immovable property during the relevant period.The ITAT Mumbai also rejected the view that the transaction involved receipt of property without consideration.The tribunal also referred to its earlier decisions in the cases of Snehalata Heramb Dhayagude, Anil Dattaram Pitale and Amar Narendra Joshi. In those matters, the tribunal had recognised that receiving alternate premises after surrendering existing tenancy or property rights does not amount to receiving immovable property either without consideration or for inadequate consideration.In this case, therefore, two fundamental requirements for applying Section 56(2)(x) were not satisfied.The first was the absence of actual receipt of the immovable property during the relevant previous year. The redevelopment project was still under construction and possession of the alternate premises had not been handed over.The second was that the transaction was not without consideration. The alternate accommodation was being provided in return for Devshichhadva surrendering his tenancy rights, which had value.The tribunal's ruling, however, is limited to the question of whether Section 56(2)(x) could be applied in these circumstances. It does not decide whether the surrender or extinguishment of the tenancy rights could have separate capital-gains tax consequences. That remains a distinct issue.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India Business News: Banks will remain open on Sunday, September 27, to ensure customers have access to banking services ahead of a proposed three-day nationwide bank stri.
articles.body: Banks will remain open on Sunday, September 27, to ensure customers have access to banking services ahead of a proposed three-day nationwide bank strike, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Wednesday.The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) has called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. The Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted,” the statement said.Why are bank unions planning a strike?The UFBU has said bank operations could be disrupted across the country during the three-day strike from September 28 to 30. Since the strike follows the weekend holidays, customers could potentially face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations are carried out.The UFBU, which claims to represent around 90% of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is concrete progress on its key demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” the UFBU said in a statement following a meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.summary: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. agreed to buy a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts International for about $3 billion, a deal that will give the cruise operator acces...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. agreed to buy a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts International for about $3 billion, a deal that will give the cruise operator access to its all-inclusive resorts across the Caribbean.

Under the deal, the two companies will form a joint venture controlling Sandals, Miami-based Royal Caribbean said Wednesday. Family members of Sandals founder Gordon Stewart, who died in 2021, will retain the other half.

The agreement comes amid another period of turmoil for the cruise industry, as the war in the Middle East dents its recovery from the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. Royal Caribbean expects to expand its offerings in the Caribbean via the Sandals tie-up by combining cruises with resort stays.

Shares of Royal Caribbean have slumped almost 16% this year, though that is less than peers Carnival Corp. and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd.

Royal Caribbean Group secured debt financing from Morgan Stanley to fund the deal, which is expected to complete in early 2027.

articles.title: Trump is turning to a Putin ally to help America’s farmers. But there’s a big catch
articles.summary: President Donald Trump’s escalating trade war with Canada has thus far spared one critical import for American farmers: potash, a crucial fertilizer component and plant nutrient that has virtually no substitute.
articles.body: President Donald Trump’s escalating trade war with Canada has thus far spared one critical import for American farmers: potash, a crucial fertilizer component and plant nutrient that has virtually no substitute. But that could change as the trade battle lingers and Canadian officials weigh options to retaliate beyond tariffs. Trump suggested this week he’s found an alternative to Canada’s stranglehold on US potash supplies: Belarus, a completely landlocked country thousands of miles away from America’s farm country that is run by a strongman ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said on Truth Social that he’s working on a “massive Deal” to buy potash from Belarus at a much cheaper price than Canada, which supplied about 90% of US potash imports last year. Trump framed the talks as “very good news for our Farmers and Ranchers.” But there are multiple obstacles to pivoting the US potash supply, including Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko’s doubts about a deal. Just hours before Trump’s post, Lukashenko said his country “cannot supply large volumes” of potash to the United States because its supplies have already been spoken for this year. The United States slapped a 50% tariff on many goods from Canada this summer – but critical imports, such as potash, crude oil and electricity, were spared. Trump’s scramble to tout the US talks with Belarus underscores the pressure from American farmers, who are slammed by surging diesel and fertilizer costs linked to the war with Iran. Some analysts doubt a deal with Belarus, a sanctioned nation thousands of miles away, would alleviate America’s long-standing reliance on Canadian potash. Canada supplied about 90% of the 13 million tons of potassium fertilizer imported last year, according to federal data. “It’s not realistic at all. It’s prohibitively expensive to remove Belarusian material,” said Alexis Maxwell, senior analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. Due to European sanctions on Belarus, Maxwell estimates that it would cost about $200 per metric ton for Belarus to deliver potash to the United States before profit margins. That’s sharply higher than the $130-per-metric-ton cost for potash from America’s neighbors to the north. In 2021, prior to import restrictions imposed on Belarus, the United States imported about 700,000 tons of potassium fertilizer from Belarus, accounting for 5% of total imports, according to federal data. Chris Krueger, global head of macro research at TD Cowen Washington Research Group, noted that Belarusian potash is already largely committed to Asia and the logistics of shipping it to the United States would be “challenging.” “We remain skeptical,” Krueger wrote in a note to clients Tuesday. Scott Lincicome, vice president of the libertarian think tank Cato Institute, was more blunt. “Look, if you can’t laugh at the president desperately promising angry farmers that he’ll magically replace massive quantities of fertilizer from our nextdoor military ally with small imaginary quantities from a tinpot authoritarian thousands of miles away, then you simply have no sense of humor,” Lincicome posted on X. Businesses are already grappling with supply chain turmoil and price hikes unleashed by the Iran war. Anything that makes it harder or more expensive to purchase Canada’s potash would make matters worse. Nitrogen-based fertilizer prices increased by 22% year-over-year in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ producer price index. Producer prices on diesel, a critical fuel that powers trucks, tractors and trains, surged by 78% in August, according to the BLS. That trend is not likely to fade as diesel continues to hit all-time highs in September. Goldman Sachs warned clients earlier this month that global food prices are at risk of going sharply higher due in part to soaring diesel and fertilizer costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis.

articles.title: What is IMEC? The India-Europe corridor in focus after Trump’s push amid Iran tensions
articles.summary: India Business News: US President Donald Trump has thrown his weight behind the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), linking the ambitious connectivity proje.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has thrown his weight behind the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), linking the ambitious connectivity project to a broader push to move Middle Eastern energy infrastructure away from routes vulnerable to Iranian pressure.Speaking at a meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council and Arab leaders on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Trump said attacks on commercial shipping had shown the need to shift energy infrastructure away from “Iranian checkpoints”. He said his administration “strongly supports” IMEC and other efforts to create alternative routes for moving oil and energy.Trump’s comments have brought fresh attention to a project announced with considerable fanfare at the G20 Summit in New Delhi in 2023, but whose progress has since been slowed by wars and instability across West Asia.What is IMEC?The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor is a proposed multinational connectivity network designed to link India with the Gulf and Europe through a combination of sea, rail, road, energy and digital infrastructure.The project has two broad sections: an Eastern Corridor, connecting India to the Arabian Gulf, and a Northern Corridor, connecting the Gulf to Europe. The proposed network would combine maritime shipping with rail and road links rather than relying entirely on a single mode of transport.The plan also envisages electricity infrastructure, digital connectivity and potentially hydrogen-related infrastructure alongside the transport network.The corridor was announced at the September 2023 G20 Summit in New Delhi. Its core participants include India, the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Israel, Jordan, France, Germany, Italy and the European Union.At its core, IMEC is intended to make the movement of goods, energy and data between India, the Middle East and Europe faster and more resilient.How would the corridor work?Instead of sending cargo entirely by sea from India to Europe through existing maritime routes, IMEC would combine shipping with overland rail connections.Goods from India would move by sea to the Gulf. From there, the proposed rail network would carry cargo across the Middle East towards the Mediterranean, where it could again move by sea into Europe.The plan also envisages supplementary road links and infrastructure for electricity, digital communications and clean energy.The Middle East Institute says the corridor could potentially reduce shipping times by up to 40% compared with traditional routes, although the eventual gains would depend on how much of the planned infrastructure is actually built and how efficiently the network operates.That multimodal design is also central to its strategic appeal: if one shipping route becomes vulnerable, cargo could have alternative land-based connections.Why has Trump linked IMEC to Iran?This is where the corridor has acquired a new significance.The Iran war has disrupted major energy and shipping routes across West Asia, including the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has argued that the region needs infrastructure that is less exposed to such chokepoints and to Iranian pressure.The proposed corridor is designed to provide an alternative route for goods and energy, although it would not simply replace the existing maritime system. Much of IMEC's infrastructure still has to be developed, and the route itself passes through a politically volatile region.The Middle East Institute notes that IMEC was originally designed to bypass vulnerable sections of the Bab al-Mandab and Suez routes through a combination of rail, ports, electricity grids and subsea cables.What does India gain?For India, IMEC is primarily about improving access to the Gulf and European markets while making supply chains more diversified.A functioning corridor could give Indian exporters another route into Europe and reduce their dependence on long maritime journeys. It could also deepen India's economic links with the UAE, Saudi Arabia and European economies.The planned digital infrastructure could connect India more closely with data networks in the Gulf and Europe, while the energy component could create new avenues for electricity and clean-energy cooperation.The corridor also fits into India's wider effort to expand its role in global connectivity and supply chains.Why isn't IMEC already operational?The biggest problem is geography, and geopolitics.The proposed route passes through a region that has been repeatedly hit by war and instability. The original concept also depended heavily on improved Saudi-Israeli ties and a stable connection through Israel and Jordan.The October 2023 Hamas attack and the wars that followed disrupted that political environment and slowed progress on the corridor. The Middle East Institute says the original form of IMEC is effectively on hold amid regional instability.There are also major infrastructure gaps. Rail links need to be developed or connected across several countries, while ports along the proposed route have different capacities and ownership structures.And there is competition. Other proposed routes, including the Iraq-Turkey-Europe Development Road, are also seeking to connect Asian and Middle Eastern markets with Europe.So Trump's endorsement does not mean IMEC is ready to start carrying cargo. The project still faces questions over funding, construction, regional security and political coordination.Why does IMEC matter now?When IMEC was announced in 2023, it was presented largely as a major trade and connectivity project linking India, the Gulf and Europe.The Iran war has given it another layer: route security.As wars and attacks expose the vulnerability of traditional energy and shipping chokepoints, the logic of having multiple routes for moving goods, energy and data has become more prominent.For India, that makes IMEC relevant not just as an infrastructure project but as a possible long-term alternative for connecting its economy with the Gulf and Europe.Trump's latest backing gives the project fresh political attention. Whether that translates into construction, however, will depend on whether the countries along the proposed route can overcome the geopolitical and infrastructure hurdles that have slowed IMEC since its launch.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Trawling fight makes waves in Alaska Senate contest
articles.summary: The race for Senate in Alaska, one of Democrats’ best hopes this year for retaking a seat in the upper chamber, has a lot to do with fish. Both candidates’ records on trawling — which refers to fishing by dragging large nets through the sea — have become a central issue in the contest and…
articles.body:
The race for Senate in Alaska, one of Democrats’ best hopes this year for retaking a seat in the upper chamber, has a lot to do with fish .

Both candidates’ records on trawling — which refers to fishing by dragging large nets through the sea — have become a central issue in the contest and a critical flash point in a state that depends largely on commercial and subsistence fishing.

As the stocks of salmon, crab and halibut run low in critical regions of the state, some Alaskans have blamed large-scale trawling, which can pick up young salmon, halibut and other fish besides their targeted species.

Former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) has staked out a campaign platform around “fish, family and freedom” in her effort to unseat incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. While attacking Sullivan’s fundraising ties to out-of-state trawling companies, Peltola has called for a crackdown on “factory trawlers” — ships that process and harvest fish on board.

“Some of the fisheries that have sustained generations of Alaskans are suffering at the hands of Lower 48 factory trawlers, and we need to take action,” Peltola said in a statement. “We’re in this fight together against out-of-state corporations who export our fish and our profits while leaving our fisheries worse off.”

Sullivan has also worked on legislation to help fisheries while in the Senate. He recently authored a bill to reduce bycatch in pollock trawling, specifically, including by setting new standards for monitoring and testing new technology that reduces seafloor disturbances. That bill passed out of the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee just last week.

But Peltola, a Native woman from the Yukon region who has worked on commercial fishing boats, has the upper hand in that she’s made a key platform out of opposition to large-scale trawling in four campaigns for Congress.

And some political observers view Sullivan’s push for trawling legislation as him playing catchup.

“It’s basically Sullivan conceding to fight this out on Mary Peltola’s turf,” said Aubrey Wieber, founder of the 907 Initiative, a government watchdog group based in Anchorage. His group also runs a website aimed at combating “Big Trawl.”

Sullivan spokesperson Nate Adams hit back, pointing to Peltola’s legislative record on fishing during her years in the House in contrast with Sullivan’s tenure.

“Mary Peltola made ‘fish’ part of four different campaigns in four years, but in Congress she never accomplished anything on fish other than printing it on a bumper sticker,” Adams said, noting that none of the bills the House Democrat introduced in her first two terms “had anything to do with fish.”

Adams cited several bills led by Sullivan on fishing and coastal resources that became law, including measures to clean up the marine coastline, crack down on illegal foreign fishing and study declining salmon populations in the state.

While the issue of factory trawling may seem hyperlocal, opposition to the industry in Alaska mirrors debate over data centers, for instance, in other battleground states.

Voters, concerned about the cost of living as well as environmental impacts in their backyard, are turning on big corporations and their most visible infrastructure — whether that’s a 2-acre data center going up in Ohio or an out-of-state trawler fleet in the Bering Sea.

Data for Progress, a Democratic-leaning group, found in 2025 that 74 percent of likely voters in Alaska support a ban on trawling. Among independent and third-party voters, 77 percent said they support such a ban.

Some in Alaska, however, have pushed back on the campaigns’ criticism of the industry despite its unpopularity.

Doug Vincent-Lang, commissioner of Alaska’s Department of Fish and Game, argued that fishing and trawling regulators have made significant progress on limiting bycatch and addressing declining stocks of fish.

“A picture is sometimes painted that trawling is the sole cause of stock declines, and that if we just ended it, all would be well,” he argued in an op-ed published by the Anchorage Daily News last week. “Unfortunately, the issue is more complex.”

Vincent-Lang specifically cited efforts to close off some regions from “bottom trawling” and institute caps for bycatch.

Regardless, growing backlash to the industry is buoyed by political forces.

A seafood executive who spoke to The Hill on the condition of anonymity said outside spending against trawling in the state has fired up Alaskans, boosting Peltola’s position while pressuring Sullivan to take a harder stance on the industry.

“There’s all this money to sort of build up a lot of noise around anti-trawl, but that never really split Republicans from Democrats in Alaska,” said the executive, adding that opposition to trawling served as a “ticket to entry” in the race.

The seafood executive pointed to the state’s open gubernatorial race in which four candidates were winnowed from 17 in an August primary. Most took an anti-trawling stance and pledged to appoint like-minded officials to regulate the industry, the executive said.

Another industry executive claimed campaigns’ focus on the industry has fueled public fervor over the issue. That executive mentioned the Facebook group STOP Alaskan Trawler Bycatch, which was founded by a recreational halibut charter captain in 2020 and boasts nearly 60,000 members.

“The Facebook group and now candidates are making the connection between abundance declines and trawl that is disconnected from reality,” the industry executive said.

“And when Alaskans hear both parties doing that, that’s when they just assume, ‘Oh, well if they’re telling us that trawl is causing these things then it must be causing those things,’ even though it’s not.”

But, for many in the state, trawling “is definitely the main issue” for Alaska voters after the economy and cost of living, Wieber said.

“Regardless of what issue is ultimately bringing people out to vote and influencing [how] they vote, this is the battle that the two Senate candidates have decided to fight for in this election,” Wieber added.

This year alone, the four leading "hyperscalers" — Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Meta ( META ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ) — are expected to spend roughly $800 billion in capital expenditures, or 10 times their spend in 2019, only seven years ago, per Goldman Sachs.

Sustaining that investment, however, will require an equally historic expansion in the cash generated by the companies footing the bill, says Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

Over the past year, the financing for the AI spending race has come increasingly from the debt market, where the hyperscalers are expected to issue $250 billion in global investment-grade debt by the end of 2026.

Pushing the hyperscalers toward the debt market is a shortage of cash. While these companies have long been known as cash juggernauts, the intense spending requirements of AI infrastructure have pushed Big Tech toward increasingly tighter cash flow. In July, Alphabet reported its first quarter of negative free cash flow since going public as Google in 2004.

Allowing this to happen, argues Sløk, are expectations that the companies that have been deploying cash are set to begin making it back in spades. Consensus estimates on Wall Street now expect operating cash flow to grow from $600 billion in 2025 to roughly $2 trillion in 2030 — more than tripling within five years, per data compiled by Apollo Global.

If that cash flow doesn't emerge, Sløk wrote to clients, the economics underpinning the dominant driver of the US stock market could quickly shift.

"If this doesn't happen, then the risk is that the AI trade weakens, with credit spreads widening, capex plans getting cut and ultimately US GDP growth slowing," Sløk wrote to clients.

The concentration risk of the US market's reliance on the AI trade played out on Monday. Spurred by gains in hyperscaler Meta and semiconductor leaders Arm and Intel, the Nasdaq Composite index surged by 2.3% to close at an all-time high, while the S&P 500 gained 1.5%.

Yet under the hood, the breadth of that strength was highly concentrated. Thirty S&P 500 stocks touched 52-week lows on Monday, versus only seven that reached a 52-week high — a sharp divergence beneath the index rally.

Outlook for AI capex is strong, Morgan Stanley analysts led by chief equity strategist Michael Wilson wrote to clients on Monday. The analysts cite robust demand for compute, AI adopters seeing evidence of the benefits of their spending, rising computer lease rates, and the potential for "material benefits to human welfare."

articles.title: Analysts Snap Longest Run of US Earnings Upgrades in Five Years
articles.summary: Equity analysts have turned net negative on the outlook for US corporate earnings for the first time in months, reflecting concerns about the effect on profi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Equity analysts have turned net negative on the outlook for US corporate earnings for the first time in months, reflecting concerns about the effect on profits of inflation and higher interest rates.

More analysts have cut rather than raised their earnings estimates for the first time in 23 weeks, ending what had been the longest run of upgrades since September 2021, according to a Citigroup Inc. index.

"The main drivers of the weakness come from consumers, both staples and discretionaries, materials and financials," said Stephan Kemper, chief investment officer at BNP Paribas Wealth Management Germany. "I think those revisions can be directly linked to a combination of higher living costs and rising energy prices."

While Wall Street analysts are broadly confident of a bumper year of earnings for America Inc., some have raised concerns about the outlook for the equity market in the near term.

Morgan Stanley strategist Michael Wilson warned earlier this week that the S&P 500 Index is at risk of dropping as much as 7% should stock valuations extend a recent decline and if further increases in energy prices prompt tighter monetary policy.

Inflation around the world will be faster than forecast in 2027, necessitating tighter monetary policy, the OECD said in a report on Wednesday. The Federal Reserve hiked US interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years in response to price pressures.

articles.title: As AI leaders warn of catastrophe, US and China shun slowdown calls
articles.summary: Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to agree to only limited cooperation on AI safety at summit.
articles.body:
As industry leaders urge a global slowdown in artificial intelligence development for the sake of humanity, the two superpowers driving the technology’s rapid advancement have given no indication they intend to hit the brakes.

The United States and China, which are locked in a fierce strategic rivalry, have each rebutted calls to slow the pace of AI development, even as industry executives and researchers stress the need for international cooperation to avoid exposing humans to catastrophic – or even existential – risks.

As US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping prepare to meet on Wednesday in Washington, DC, for the third time this year, expectations for cooperation on AI safety are modest. Observers anticipated measures that, at best, would fall far short of the coordinated slowdown that many experts said is needed.

“The two countries host nearly all frontier labs and most of the models people download,” said Alvin Wang Graylin, a senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis, describing agreed guardrails between the US and China as “close to a precondition” for safe AI.

“A safety regime covering one side’s models covers half the problem,” Wang Graylin said.

Hampering the prospects for US-China cooperation, analysts said, are mutual mistrust and divergent perceptions of the primary risks involved.

Trump has dismissed fears about AI as a “conspiracy” and suggested guardrails are not needed under his leadership, stressing the need for the US to stay ahead of China in the frontier technology.

Trump, who has cast AI dominance as crucial to the US maintaining its position as the top global power, on Tuesday again poured cold water on hopes for international cooperation, telling the United Nations General Assembly that Washington would oppose any “globalist scheme” to control AI.

China has taken a more hands-on approach to AI regulation – releasing the third iteration of its security framework this month – but has similarly rebuffed calls for a slowdown, dismissing fears of existential risks aired in Silicon Valley as “fearmongering”.

While Chinese officials have raised concerns about the dangers of AI, they have related it to more prosaic concerns, including cybersecurity and the authority of the ruling Communist Party.

In a rare essay this month, Chinese Minister of State Security Chen Yixin warned of “hostile forces” using AI to “fabricate political rumours” and “incite antagonistic sentiments”, threatening “political security, institutional security and ideological security”.

“China also increasingly recognises loss of control, misuse and cyber-risks but is much more sensitive to the possibility that ‘AI safety’ could become a justification for restricting Chinese access to chips, computers or markets,” said Sun Chenghao, a fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing.

“So the deepest obstacle is whether both sides can separate genuine safety cooperation from the wider technology competition,” Sun said.

“If every safety discussion is linked to export controls or slowing China’s development, Beijing will naturally question the purpose of cooperation,” Sun added.

So far, the only proposals publicly floated by either side have been a US-China dialogue and a notification mechanism for reporting national security threats.

While those measures would be positive first steps, the US and China would still need to reach an agreement on the AI capabilities or uses that should be off-limits to avert the greatest threats, experts said.

There is no consensus within the AI sector about how the technology should be regulated – or even whether government-led supervision is needed at all.

While AI leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have called for a slowdown and greater regulation, some experts argued that such calls do not go far enough and development should be paused outright.

“International coordination is absolutely critical. We need more than safeguards,” said David Krueger, an assistant professor at the University of Montreal who specialises in AI safety.

“We need an immediate, indefinite international moratorium on frontier AI development.”

Other key figures, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, have played down the need for external oversight and emphasised AI’s potential to deliver transformative benefits for society.

Among those most alarmed at the rapid pace of AI development, recursive self-improvement, which describes when AI models learn to improve themselves, is often identified as a critical tipping point.

In an essay this month urging the AI sector to “pace the frontier”, Amodei said the US and China should discuss an agreement to “substantially limit” the rate of AI development while acknowledging that any deal is unlikely given the potential for a rule-breaking party to shift the global balance of power.

“The US and China must agree on AI capabilities red lines that will not be crossed. Most crucially, AI must never get powerful enough for recursive self-improvement,” said Otto Barten, director of the Netherlands-based Existential Risk Observatory.

“We do not know where the positive feedback loop of ever-smarter AIs creating ever-smarter AIs without human supervision will end and what these agents will finally be able to do,” Barten added.

Wang Graylin said Washington and Beijing should come to an agreement on what constitutes an “unacceptable capability” and a common standard to test frontier models, ideally by an independent international body that is funded by multiple countries.

But Wang Graylin acknowledged that distrust is clouding the prospects for an agreement and US officials are likely to see any deal as impossible to verify.

“Verification is hard for software you cannot see,” he said.

Sun said the US could ease the path to cooperation by “drawing a clearer line” between policies aimed at AI safety and those intended to maintain Washington’s technological advantage.

China could also contribute to greater trust by providing “greater transparency about its safety practices, model-evaluation methods and incident-reporting mechanisms,” Sun said.

Henry Gao, an expert on China and trade law at Singapore Management University, said a deeper issue is a fundamental mismatch in how Washington and Beijing view AI risks.

“Many in the US AI-safety debate focus on the possibility of highly capable AI escaping human control and posing catastrophic risks to humanity,” Gao said.

“In China, national security concerns appear more geopolitical: A major perceived danger is that the US could gain a decisive AI advantage and use it against China,” Gao said.

“That creates pressure to accelerate rather than slow development.”

Some AI experts argued that the focus of a US-China dialogue should be on mitigating existing risks rather than slowing development outright.

“AI is already extremely useful and has the potential to improve lives around the world,” said Rui Ma, a tech industry consultant and the founder of the Tech Buzz China news site, adding that pausing development would also impact the technology’s positive applications.

“I think thoughtful rules of engagement, constant monitoring, open channels of communication and the ability to adjust our approach as AI acquires different capabilities are much more important,” Ma said.

“The safeguards need to evolve alongside the technology.”

Calling the upcoming talks between Trump and Xi a “positive signal”, Jiang Tianjiao, associate professor at the Development Institute at Fudan University in Shanghai, expressed hope the sides could overcome their geopolitical rivalry to find common ground.

“China and the US are currently the leading nations in AI development,” Jiang said. “As such, we bear the responsibility of major powers to prevent AI from spiralling out of control, and we should set a global example by cooperating to manage these risks.”
